verses.text: While David was king, there was a famine for three years in a row. So David asked the LORD about it. The LORD said, "It is because of Saul and his family. They are guilty of murder, because Saul killed the Gibeonites."

So the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. The Gibeonites were not Israelites. They were what was left of the Amorites. The Israelites had promised with an oath to spare them, but Saul had tried to wipe them out because he was so eager to help the people of Israel and Judah.
David asked the Gibeonites, "What can I do for you? How can I make up for the wrong that was done, so that you will bless the LORD's people?"
The Gibeonites answered him, "We do not want silver or gold from Saul or his family. And we do not have the right to put anyone in Israel to death." David said, "I will do whatever you ask."
They answered the king, "Saul tried to destroy us. He planned to wipe us out so that we would have no place anywhere in Israel.
So hand over seven of his male descendants to us. We will hang them in front of the LORD at Gibeah, Saul's town, the town of the man the LORD chose." The king said, "I will hand them over."
But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul, because of the promise David and Jonathan had made to each other in front of the LORD.

Instead, the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul. He also took the five sons Saul's daughter Merab had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai from Meholah.

He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged them on a hill in front of the LORD. All seven of them died together. They were put to death in the first days of the harvest, just as the barley harvest was beginning.

Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until the rain fell on the bodies. She did not let the birds land on them during the day or the wild animals come near them at night.
When David was told what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's slave wife, had done,

he went and got the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the people of Jabesh Gilead. They had secretly taken the bodies from the public square in Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them up after they killed Saul on Mount Gilboa.
David brought the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from there, and they also gathered up the bones of the seven men who had been hanged.

They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the tomb of Saul's father Kish, at Zela in the land of Benjamin. They did everything the king commanded. After that, God answered their prayers for the land.
Once again there was war between the Philistines and Israel. David went down with his men to fight the Philistines, and he became very tired.

Ishbi-Benob, one of the descendants of the giants, had a bronze spear tip that weighed three hundred shekels, about three and a half kilograms. He was wearing new armour, and he planned to kill David.

But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David's rescue. He struck the Philistine and killed him. Then David's men made him promise, "You must never go out with us to battle again. You are the lamp of Israel, and we must not let that light go out."
Some time later there was another battle with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbekai from Hushah killed Saph, another descendant of the giants.
In another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim from Bethlehem killed the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear had a shaft as thick as the bar on a weaver's loom.
There was another battle at Gath. A huge man was there who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all. He too was a descendant of the giants.
When he made fun of Israel, Jonathan son of Shimei, David's brother, killed him.
These four were descendants of the giants in Gath, and they were killed by David and his men.
